description.value: The study investigated neural mechanisms of attention-to-breath during aversive emotional stimulation, focusing on amygdala activation, prefrontal activation, and emotion-related amygdala–prefrontal functional connectivity.

spans.text: Functional MRI and visual–emotional stimulation with and without ATB was used to investigate brain mechanisms that underlie emotion regulation effects of ATB.

value: We hypothesized first that brain activation effects of ATB and visual–emotional stimulation interact in prefrontal areas and amygdala.
Secondly, we proposed that, during emotional stimulation, ATB down-regulates activation in the amygdala and increases its integration with prefrontal regions.

description.value: 26 healthy participants were trained in mindfulness-based attention-to-breath meditation for two weeks and then underwent fMRI while performing an emotional picture task under attention-to-breath and passive-viewing conditions.

spans.text: To address this hypothesis, 26 healthy controls were trained in mindfulness-based attention-to-breath meditation for two weeks and then stimulated with aversive pictures during both attention-to-breath and passive viewing while undergoing fMRI.
During fMRI, participants expected and perceived cued aversive pictures under two continuous conditions, i.e., ATB and passive viewing (PV).
